findings.obs_text: In Job 1:9 answered (H6030B) opens the verse, six words before for no reason: the question whether Job's fear has a cause is Satan's answer to the Lord.

In Pro 3:30 contend (H7378) stands two words before for no reason, which qualifies it: the strife forbidden is strife without cause. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through argue, a synonym; the verse pairs the reason with contend instead.
findings.grounds: Do not contend with a man for no reason

findings.obs_text: In Jam 3:17 peaceable (G1516) stands two places before open to reason in the list of the qualities of the wisdom from above.
findings.grounds: then peaceable, gentle, open to reason

findings.obs_text: In 1Pe 3:15 prepared (G2092) stands six words before reason: the readiness is to make a defense to the one who asks for the reason; the reason is what the believer is ready to give.
findings.grounds: always being prepared to make a defense

findings.obs_text: In Act 18:14 accept (G0430) stands directly after reason, which governs it: Gallio would have ground to hear the complaint out, under the condition of a crime; the reason is the ground for accepting.
findings.grounds: I would have reason to accept your complaint

findings.obs_text: In Dan 4:34 and Dan 4:36 returned (H8421G) stands directly after reason as its verb: the reason is the subject that comes back to the king; in Dan 4:36 the same verb then carries his glory, majesty and splendor back as well.
In Eze 19:10 abundant (H7227A) stands directly after by reason of and describes the water named as the cause of the vine's fruitfulness. The data gives the word reason here the code H1961 (to be).
In Act 24:25 righteousness (G1343) stands two words after reasoned and is the first subject of the reasoning: Paul reasons about righteousness.
In 1Ti 1:16 perfect (G3956) stands eight words after for this reason and describes the patience shown, not the reason.

older.finding: righteousness as godliness, devoutness or uprightness of a person
older.reason: it states a face of the righteousness words; the righteous collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Dan 4:36 sought (H1156) stands thirteen words after reason, in the sequence that follows its return: the king's counselors and lords seek him out again.
findings.grounds: My counselors and my lords sought me

findings.obs_text: In Act 10:21 looking for (G2212) stands two words before reason: the men's seeking of Peter comes first, and Peter then asks the reason for their coming; the reason asked explains the seeking.
findings.grounds: I am the one you are looking for

older.finding: zeteo in Acts 10:19 and 10:21 in its plain sense of looking for a person
older.reason: it states the sense of the search word; the search collection owns it

older.mapping: it says reason and seeking stand together in Acts 10:21, the seeking first and Peter's asking of the reason after it; the finding of this row on Act 10:21 states the same
older.reason: the pairing finding of this row on Act 10:21 carries it

older.finding: the seeking in Acts 10:21 is done by the men and directed toward Peter
older.reason: it states the parties of the search word; the search collection owns it

older.finding: sought names a physical, practical or record search in these verses
older.reason: it states the use of the search word; the search collection owns it

older.finding: looking for in Acts 10:19 and 10:21 is an outward search for a person
older.reason: it states the use of the search word; the search collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Act 24:25 self-control (G1466) stands four words after reasoned and is the second subject of the reasoning, between righteousness and the judgment to come. The data gives the word a second code at the same place, G2532 (and).
In 1Cor 13:11 gave up (G2673) stands six words after reasoned, in the next sentence: as a man the speaker set aside childish ways, the speaking, thinking and reasoning of the child among them.
In Num 18:32 sin (H2399) stands directly before by reason of it: the giver will carry no sin, and the reason phrase names the contribution as why.
findings.grounds: you shall bear no sin by reason of it

findings.obs_text: In Isa 1:18 sins (H2399) stands four words after reason, in what the reasoning together concerns: sins red as scarlet made white as snow. The data gives the word a second code at the same place, H1961 (to be).
findings.grounds: though your sins are like scarlet

findings.obs_text: In 1Jo 3:8 sinning (G0266, G0264) stands nine and three words before the reason: the sinning of the devil from the beginning is what the purpose the reason introduces is aimed against.
findings.grounds: the devil has been sinning from the beginning

older.finding: the charge of Isaiah 1 goes to the inner being: rebellion, not knowing, the heart faint, worship refused
older.reason: it states how the people's inner being is charged in Isaiah 1; its words are of many collections, sin among them
it states how the will is invited in Isa 1:18-20, where the reasoning together is this subgroup's word; inner being, answered at step 3.1

findings.obs_text: In Luk 9:47 took (G1949) stands three words after reasoning: knowing their reasoning, Jesus takes a child; his act answers the reasoning he knows.
findings.grounds: took a child and put him by his side

findings.obs_text: In Act 19:9 took (G0873) stands two words before reasoning: Paul takes the disciples apart, and then reasons daily in the hall; the taking aside comes before the new place of reasoning.
findings.grounds: took the disciples with him, reasoning daily

findings.obs_text: In 1Th 3:7 distress (G2347) and affliction (G0318) stand five and seven words after for this reason, in the clause it governs: the comfort came in the midst of their distress and affliction.
findings.grounds: in all our distress and affliction

older.finding: longing both ways, and comfort in distress and affliction (1Th 3:6-7)
older.reason: it states how longing and comfort work in distress; the tribulation collection owns it
